features.title: New thread prepares its destination while the draft is written
features.summary: The sidebar's New thread, the palette and the project picker open the composer at once and claim nothing: with isolation on by default the blank thread waits in the project (or inherited) checkout. Once its draft holds something, the destination is prepared in the background (the jj workspace claimed, its blank Session connected) so the first send copies the draft and submits instead of waiting for both; the send still holds the composer until that Session is open. The created thread takes the view only while this New thread screen is the visible main view, and is otherwise offered in a toast. An abandoned draft keeps the prepared workspace as the project's spare, which a reload or the next New thread reuses. A thread left in another thread's workspace moves back to the project checkout on arrival when isolation is off, which creates nothing.

features.title: Integrate a thread into the bookmark
features.summary: One conversation-header control names the current thread's jj workspace, how many revisions are ready to integrate, and whether integration is blocked; its menu holds Integrate, the Thread workspaces side panel, and Download session log. Hovering the current-thread workspace chip lazily previews a bounded revision graph of thread work, the configured bookmark and its origin ref, plus the default workspace. Integrate a thread's described work into the target bookmark from that menu, the panel, the newest completed turn, or the compatible `/rebase` composer command. The turn-end row names the pending revisions and offers the same Integrate one click from the answer the user just read; it disappears once the work lands. Under the hood, jj rebases thread revisions onto the current bookmark tip, then advances the bookmark; existing bookmark ancestry stays intact. The in-chat notice shows the tip change ID and offers the configured follow-up action for the current thread. Queueing or cancelling an integration leaves a dated chat notice; the active queued notice offers Undo, and a subtle thread-list tag disappears when cancelled or completed. Queue notices share the Host-memory lifetime of the queue. Integration refuses non-thread workspaces and is disabled while any thread session is working or waiting for input; an agent handed back conflicts or descriptions may integrate its own thread once they are fixed, while every other session of that thread must still be idle. Afterwards the checkout running DSH follows the bookmark in the background through `dshx checkout sync`, with a panel line saying what was rebuilt and whether to restart.

The rebase notice offers the actions `integratedThreadActions` selects; Archive affects only the current Session and both actions are disabled while it runs, while Settle is answered by thread-sidebar, the owner of the settled status.
The post-rebase checkout sync refuses described work the bookmark lacks and undoes a conflicting rebase; the panel line names the files and the rebase itself stands.

A refused checkout sync is a safe no-change outcome, not a failure: the panel line says the checkout was kept as is with its local work preserved and gives dshx's next step, in default styling, and Activity records it as `workspace.sync_refused`; conflicts and build failures stay destructive `workspace.sync_failed`.

Only the newest completed turn offers the inline Integrate: an older turn keeps its dated notices, and the row is hidden for a shared checkout, an archived thread, a queued or running integration, unverified activity, or work the control center calls blocked (undescribed, conflicted, missing).

features.title: Thread integration control center
features.summary: A full-page control center, also in the conversation side panel: state tabs with live counts, a separate lifecycle filter, and a banner whose primary action integrates every ready workspace at once. Integration state (ready, blocked, conflicts, integrating, integrated, no changes, unverified) is kept separate from lifecycle (active, idle, finished, missing), so a workspace that merely sits behind the bookmark is 'no changes', never a blocker. Empty sections are not rendered while their counts stay in the filter bar. Rows prioritise the conversation title (falling back to the pending revision description, then the project name), the specific blocker, the pending-versus-behind distinction and a contextual action; workspace and thread ids stay secondary and copyable. Batch integration enqueues ready workspaces serially through the existing coordinator, and the queue line names what is active, queued or failed.
